open.thesis: 84% rostered nationally and dropped by Footballers — an ownership anomaly, not a bad player. Listed WR1 for Jacksonville ahead of Meyers.
open.falsifiedIf: Target share stays under about 18% through week 3, or Meyers/Washington pass him on the depth chart.
open.review: Week 1 reviewed 14 Sep, UNRESOLVED and trending against. Thomas went 3 of 3 for 40 with no touchdown while Lawrence threw four, and Jacksonville's first official depth chart of 2026 lists Parker Washington in the top receiver slot; Washington led the team with 5 for 83 and a score. Two mitigations: Lawrence attempted only 23 passes and was pulled leading 34-3, and Thomas took a shoulder knock in the second quarter and returned. The falsification condition is deliberately left as written - it measures target share through week 3 and one blowout is not three weeks. No action taken; he was added 12 Sep and the churn rule closes that slot. If week 2 brings another sub-18% target share, this closes as WRONG.

open.thesis: Pittsburgh's listed RB1 and the primary passing-down back. Chem switched to full PPR, which doubles the value of the receiving edge that had made him a sit.
open.falsifiedIf: Dowdle out-touches him materially two weeks running, or Warren's target share drops below Dowdle's.
open.review: Week 1 reviewed 14 Sep, HELD and strengthened by a fact the thesis did not have. Pittsburgh's depth chart lists Warren RB1 and Dowdle RB2, and Kenneth Gainwell - the man who took the passing-down snaps - was traded to Tampa Bay, so the receiving work the full-PPR argument rests on is now uncontested. Warren returned 10.3 on a 12.6 projection, which is neither evidence for nor against.

open.thesis: Reconstructed after the fact from reporting. Likely signed 3yr/$40M to follow Harbaugh from Baltimore and is the undisputed Giants TE1 and primary slot option, with Nabers coming off an ACL and a receiver room only four deep.
open.falsifiedIf: Nabers returns to full health and Likely's route share drops below about 60%, or Theo Johnson takes the 11-personnel snaps back.
open.review: Week 1 reviewed 14 Sep, HELD emphatically. 8 targets, 8 catches, 78 yards, two touchdowns, 27.8 PPR, best of any tight end in the early window. Reporting confirms the reconstructed thesis: three years and $40M, full-time tight end for the first time in his career, and Nabers still not fully integrated into the offence. Acted on this run by starting him over Pitts rather than by any roster move.

open.thesis: 8 of 9 for 138 and two scores, led Carolina in every receiving category while McMillan was quiet until garbage time. 50% rostered is an anomaly in a ten-team league. Chem priority resets weekly so the claim is free.
open.falsifiedIf: McMillan reasserts as the clear alpha and Coker's target share falls under about 18% across weeks 2-3, or the week 1 line proves to have been garbage-time inflated.
open.review: Still pending; the claim does not process until Wednesday 07:00 UTC, so it cannot resolve before then. Re-researched rather than recycled: Coker led Carolina in snaps (57) and routes run (40), ahead of McMillan's 56 and 39. That is the full-time role the thesis assumed and it is now measured rather than inferred. Sports Illustrated still call McMillan the primary target, which is the live counter-argument.

open.thesis: Start Likely over Pitts from week 2. This overrides ESPN's own season projection, which prefers Pitts 181.4 to 156.2 and ranks him TE7 to Likely's TE12. The override is on role, not on week 1: Likely is a full-time tight end for the first time on a three-year $40M deal with Nabers still ramping back in, while Pitts played a full game and was not targeted for a catch.
open.falsifiedIf: Pitts out-scores Likely in two of the next three weeks, or Nabers returns to full health and Likely's route share drops below about 60%, or Theo Johnson takes the 11-personnel snaps back.

closed.summary: One bench slot went Goedert -> Allgeier -> Likely in five days. Each step was defensible on projection; the sequence gained nothing and cost two roster moves.
Recommended dropping Kyle Monangai for Tre Tucker on 13 Sep. Monangai returned from the knee and scored 20.4; Tucker's Bowers-vacuum thesis now has a return date on it. Not acted on.

A 13 Sep run recommended adding Xavier Worthy and dropping Isaiah Likely, on the reasoning that a second TE is structurally unplayable in a RB/WR flex. Likely then scored 27.8 with two touchdowns. The structural argument was sound and the conclusion was still wrong, because it valued the slot rather than the player.
